newsitem.title: USA: Likely Maine Reform Party candidate drops out.
newsitem.headline: Likely Maine Reform Party candidate drops out.

text.p: The independent who was expected to represent Ross Perot's Reform Party in Maine's U.S. Senate race dropped out of the contest Tuesday for lack of money and support.
Steve Bost, Perot's New England political director until he entered the Senate race, said he realized while campaigning this summer that he was not going to be competitive in the five-way contest.
"I saw the handwriting on the wall," said Bost, a former Democratic lawmaker who directed Perot's campaign to a second place showing in Maine in the 1992 presidential race.
The Reform Party was expected to endorse Bost, who ran as an independent because the party was not officially recognized in Maine at the time candidates signed up for the Senate race.
His departure leaves four candidates: Republican Susan Collins, Democrat Joe Brennan and independents John Ressenbrink, an environmentalist, and William Clarke, a Christian fundamentalist.
